title: To cut a long story short
description: To give only the main outcome.
details:
Example: To cut a long story short, we missed the train.

Usage: Conversational; skip less important details.

title: It all started when
details:
Example: It all started when I lost my keys.

Usage: Neutral; introduce the first event.

title: Out of the blue
details:
Example: She called me out of the blue.

Usage: Conversational; describe a surprise.

title: Before I knew it
details:
Example: Before I knew it, the week was over.

Usage: Neutral; emphasise how quickly time passed.

title: One thing led to another
description: Events developed into an unexpected result.
details:
Example: One thing led to another, and we started a band.

Usage: Conversational; summarise a chain of events.

title: As luck would have it
details:
Example: As luck would have it, a taxi appeared.

Usage: Neutral; the context determines whether luck was good.

title: To make matters worse
details:
Example: To make matters worse, my phone died.

Usage: Neutral; add a worsening development.

title: Much to my surprise
details:
Example: Much to my surprise, he apologised.

Usage: Neutral; emphasise your reaction.

title: In the meantime
description: During the wait for something else.
details:
Example: Dinner will be ready soon; in the meantime, sit down.

Usage: Neutral; simultaneous or intervening activity.

title: All of a sudden
details:
Example: All of a sudden, the lights went out.

Usage: Neutral; introduce a sudden change.

title: Looking back
details:
Example: Looking back, I should have asked for help.

Usage: Neutral; introduce reflection.

title: At the time
details:
Example: At the time, I thought it was sensible.

Usage: Neutral; contrast past understanding with the present.

title: The next thing I knew
description: The next event I became aware of.
details:
Example: The next thing I knew, we were at the station.

Usage: Conversational; a rapid or surprising transition.

title: It turned out to be
description: It was eventually discovered to be.
details:
Example: It turned out to be the wrong address.

Usage: Neutral; reveal an outcome or identity.

title: I ended up
details:
Example: I ended up walking home.

Usage: Neutral; usually follow with an -ing form.

title: By the time
details:
Example: By the time we arrived, the shop had closed.

Usage: Neutral; relate the timing of two events.

title: From that point on
details:
Example: From that point on, I cycled to work.

Usage: Neutral; mark a lasting change.

title: Against all odds
description: Despite very unlikely chances of success.
details:
Example: Against all odds, we won the match.

Usage: Neutral; emphasise overcoming major difficulty.

title: That was the last straw
description: That final problem exhausted my patience.
details:
Example: Another cancelled train was the last straw.

Usage: Conversational; after several earlier frustrations.

title: It was a blessing in disguise
details:
Example: Missing that job was a blessing in disguise.

Usage: Conversational; explain an unexpectedly good consequence.
